newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lipponen repeats Finland to meet all EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Lipponen repeats Finland to meet all EMU criteria.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen repeated on Thursday that Finland would meet all criteria for joining EMU and said there was no need to revise the policy of low interest rates and a tight fiscal stance.
"The economic policy guarantees that Finland will meet the requirements for the third stage of EMU," Lipponen told a news conference.
"There is reason to continue with the combination of a policy of low interest rates and a tight fiscal stance," he said.

"The Finnish economy is growing strongly," he said, pointing to forecasts of four percent growth in 1997. "It seems that if there would be a need to revise these forecasts, any revision would be upwards, not down."
"Economic growth is on a solid base and inflation pressures scant," he said. The current account had a structural surplus.
The fall in the unemployment rate would accelerate, he said.
"Unemployment will fall significantly this year ... to around 15 percent, even a shade below ... Already now, we can project that the fall in unemployment will continue in 1998 and 1999."
But the fall was still painfully slow, he added.
Lipponen said the government had brought the rise in state indebtedness under control.
"The state finances will not require new cuts in social security or in state transfers to municipalities," he said.
Lipponen also said he expected "genuine will to reach a consensus solution behind which all government parties could stand" in an upcoming vote of confidence.
The government lost a parliamentary vote in December on liberalising retail opening hours but Lipponen vowed to reintroduce the proposal in February.
"The key issue is that the proposal will be approved," he said.
